target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2023 disclosure (D046) covers Symantec endpoint security solutions that prevent, detect, and respond to threats. The 2024 disclosure (D043) covers the 'Application Networking and Security Software Portfolio' which includes zero-trust lateral security and Advanced Threat Prevention to combat malware and ransomware. While the specific product name changed from 'Symantec endpoint security' to the broader 'Application Networking and Security' portfolio with 'Lateral Security Firewall', both address cybersecurity threat prevention and detection across infrastructure.

The 2023 disclosure (D047) covers Network Security solutions to stop inbound/outbound threats. The 2024 disclosure (D043) covers Application Networking and Security software, which includes zero-trust lateral security and Advanced Threat Prevention. Both disclosures address network/application level security threats and protection against malware/ransomware.

Network security solutions protect email and web access using advanced threat protection technologies to stop inbound and outbound threats targeting users and infrastructure.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD Solarflare offers low-latency networking solutions using hardware adapters and Onload libraries, serving as the preferred solution for capital markets high-performance applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose networking solutions, but they target different market segments and architectural needs. AVGO focuses on application-level networking and security software for zero-trust lateral security and load balancing to combat malware. In contrast, AMD's Solarflare offering is a hardware and low-latency user-space networking solution specifically optimized for capital markets and high-performance computing applications, prioritizing speed over the security/access control features emphasized by AVGO.

sentences.text: Our application networking and security software delivers zero-trust lateral security and load balancing solutions enabling global digital organizations to combat malware and ransomware.

• Lateral Security Firewall: This solution enables access control for applications, protects against lateral movement of threats and provides security policy recommendations based on the workloads, and enables isolation of sensitive applications for enhanced regulatory compliance.
The AMD Solarflare™ portfolio offers a comprehensive low latency networking solution that combines hardware adapters with the Onload™ family of user space networking libraries.
AMD Solarflare products are the preferred networking solution for capital markets, enabling customers to develop a wide range of high-performance applications across the entire trading ecosystem.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product competitiveness strategy and xPU vision
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel intensifies investment in areas key to product competitiveness, aiming to improve user experiences through advances in performance, power, cost, and security. The company believes the future lies in xPU across diverse architectures (CPU, GPU, NPU, etc.) enabled by scalable software and advanced packaging.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address security and competitiveness in their product strategies, but at different layers of the stack. AVGO explicitly integrates security (zero-trust, threat prevention) as a core software feature to protect applications and data. Intel's disclosure focuses on broader product competitiveness drivers including security as one of several attributes (alongside performance, power, and cost) for its hardware/xPU platforms, without detailing specific security product suites in this context.

sentences.text: Our application networking and security software delivers zero-trust lateral security and load balancing solutions enabling global digital organizations to combat malware and ransomware.

• Advanced Threat Prevention: This solution integrates multiple threat detection and prevention technologies to deliver comprehensive protection from malware and ransomware attacks, including utilizing behavior-based techniques and advanced correlations to identify lateral threat movement and ransomware threat campaigns.
Our objective with each new generation of products is to improve user experiences and value through advances in performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor, and other features.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight security features as part of their high-performance data center offerings for AI workloads, though their primary product categories differ. AVGO provides software-defined security solutions (firewalls, threat prevention) for application networking. Micron provides hardware storage solutions (SSDs) that include integrated security features alongside performance and power efficiency for data center operators.

comparisons.peer_summary: Leading cloud service providers and consumer internet companies use NVIDIA platforms for AI solutions, search, and social networking. Enterprises and startups across industries use the platforms for generative AI products, autonomous driving, drug discovery, and fraud detection. Researchers use the solutions for scientific applications like climate forecasting and genomics, powering over 75% of TOP500 supercomputers.
comparisons.comparison: While both companies serve the infrastructure software and hardware landscape, their focus areas diverge significantly. AVGO's disclosure centers on specific application networking and security software capabilities (lateral movement prevention). NVIDIA's disclosure focuses on the breadth of its customer base and AI compute use cases (cloud, enterprise, research), without detailing specific security networking software products in this section.

comparisons.peer_topic: Additional technologies for mobile, XR, and automotive industries
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm develops technologies for WLAN, Bluetooth, location, multimedia, and security. It also provides XR platform features (e.g., 6DoF tracking), automotive platform features (digital cockpit, ADAS), memory/controllers, fast charging, Smart Transmit technology, and power management systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies include security as a component of their broader technology portfolios, but the scope and application differ. AVGO provides enterprise-grade network security software (Lateral Security Firewall, Advanced Threat Prevention) for data center infrastructure. Qualcomm lists security systems as one of many 'additional technologies' supporting its mobile, automotive, and edge devices, focusing on device-level security and content protection rather than network-wide security architectures.
